name: áes dána

attributes.attribute: means a group of nationally acclaimed artists in modern Ireland
derives from the Old Irish term for poets

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
Áes dána, also written aos dana or aes dana, is an Irish phrase for a hero or heroine. In modern Ireland, the phrase designates a group of nationally acclaimed artists. It derives from the Old Irish term for poets. The term was also sometimes applied to Druids, Brehons, or lawyers.

In Old Irish, the áes dána were the learned classes. They helped shape the common spoken and literary language of their day. Their knowledge held a high place in the culture.

To gain the gift of inspiration, one had to drink from the Well of wisdom. One might eat the hazel nuts floating there. One might taste the flesh of the salmon that swam in it. Each act was thought to pass on the power of poetic knowledge.

The Well of wisdom and its hazel nuts appear throughout Irish lore. The salmon that swam in the well held the same wisdom. Anyone who tasted its flesh took in that insight. This path to inspiration served poets, Druids, and judges alike.

The term unites these roles under one idea. All drew on the same source of insight. All served the community through knowledge. The modern meaning, a group of acclaimed artists, keeps that older sense alive.

Today the phrase honors those who create and guard the culture. It remembers that Irish art grew from the well of learning. The poets who drank from it set the standard for those who follow.
objective: To explain the meaning and origin of the Irish phrase áes dána.
key_results: In modern Ireland the phrase means a group of nationally acclaimed artists.
It derives from the Old Irish term for poets.
It was also applied to Druids, Brehons, or lawyers.
Inspiration came from the Well of wisdom, its hazel nuts, or the salmon that swam in it.
In Old Irish the áes dána were the learned classes who shaped the common literary language.
evidence: The phrase áes dána derives from the Old Irish term for poets and was also applied to Druids, Brehons, or lawyers.
